title: Crestline Fleet Account Remittance Application Terms
content:
These terms govern how a remittance from the business is applied on a Crestline Fleet Account, and the conditions of the early-pay discount that remain in force.

### Applying a remittance

A remittance is applied to the invoices it names. When the program requires remittance advice, a remittance that names no invoice is held unapplied until the business identifies the invoices; otherwise it is applied oldest invoice first. Each part applied to one invoice is its own entry and never exceeds the amount still open on that invoice — the invoice amount less the remittances, early-pay discounts and credit memos already applied to it. A short payment leaves the difference open on the invoice.

### Early-pay discount: clauses retired

> The early-pay discount is credited on an invoice only when the remittance pays it in full.

This clause is **no longer in force** as an unqualified rule. The current basis reads: the early-pay discount is credited on the invoice the most recent remittance was applied to when that remittance arrived no later than the end of the early-pay period and, together with the payments, early-pay discounts and credit memos already applied to the invoice, leaves nothing open on it beyond the amount under an open dispute registered for that invoice and the early-pay discount itself (a remittance that already deducted the discount pays the invoice in full); every other invoice remains under the clause above.

> The discount is the program's early-pay discount percent of the invoice amount, rounded half up to the cent.

This clause is **no longer in force**. It is superseded by the current basis, under which the discount is the early-pay rate in percent applied once to the discount base, rounded half up to the cent only on that final product.

### Early-pay discount: clauses in force

- **Time condition.** The payment must be received no later than the end of the early-pay period counted from the invoice date of the invoice paid. Calendar days are counted from the day after the anchor date, so the anchor date plus the number of days is the last qualifying date. The anchor is the invoice date recorded on the invoice paid; a payment received on the last qualifying date qualifies.
- A program whose early-pay discount percent is 0 gives none.
- A full payment that already deducted the discount is applied as a payment plus a discount entry.
- Credit memos already on the invoice reduce what must be paid in full but not the discount base.

### Boundary cases (hypothetical dates, a program with an early-pay period of 10 days)

| Invoice date | Payment received | Last qualifying date | Within the period? |
|---|---|---|---|
| the 5th | the 15th | the 15th | yes (on the boundary day) |
| the 5th | the 16th | the 15th | no |
| the 5th | the 9th | the 15th | yes |

superseded_clauses: The early-pay discount is credited on an invoice only when the remittance pays it in full.
The discount is early_pay_discount_pct percent of the invoice amount, rounded half up to the cent
